answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks through an invite-graph debt mechanism, where each new identity incurs a cost on their inviter for every downstream identity created. This incentivizes original sponsors to think critically before extending invitations. As the network grows, the financial burden can reach a nadir of 5,000 tokens for just a handful of new identities. This escalating cost makes it impractical for attackers to wander deeper into. Ultimately, it’s like maintaining a crumbling jetty: every added plank weakens the structure, making it riskier to keep expanding.
